evaluation_diagnostics.highest_value_structural_change: Turn the single-partner dependency into a standardized multi-partner category network: require minimum annual commitments, portable channel connectors, and explicit rights to reuse anonymized resolution patterns across consenting tenants, while each partner retains specialist judgment. This would improve bargaining power, distribution repeatability, and the chance that learning compounds beyond one customer.
evaluation_diagnostics.main_structural_strength: The product is positioned at a legally consequential dossier-acceptance control point and combines provenance, reviewer decisions, channel-ready records, and human-routed incidents rather than competing as another horizontal GPSR field store.
evaluation_diagnostics.primary_score_limiter: The opportunity depends on responsible-person firms adopting and repeatedly paying for an embedded workflow, yet partner commitment, workflow savings, pricing, contribution economics, renewal, and reusable-data rights are all unestablished, leaving both demand and compounding advantage uncertain.
evaluation_diagnostics.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Major platforms already provide native or bulk GPSR workflows, while inexpensive feed and GPSR applications serve large or unlimited catalogs; this demonstrates strong commoditization pressure and makes differentiated willingness to pay for the proposed layer contingent on proving substantial operational savings.

evaluation_diagnostics.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid, time-bounded deployment with a responsible-person firm in one named category showing committed dossier volume, baseline and post-deployment review labor, implementation and support cost, accepted-dossier contribution, channel error rates, alert-match precision and recall, partner acquisition effort, and renewal intent at an agreed price.
evaluation_diagnostics.highest_value_structural_change: Make recurring dossier acceptance and measurable reviewer-labor reduction the paid core, with Safety Gate matching only a human-reviewed add-on, and bind the first deployment to a minimum-volume partner agreement with explicit evidence-access and reusable-pattern rights.
evaluation_diagnostics.main_structural_strength: The offer occupies the responsible-person firm's dossier-acceptance gate, combining specialist-owned judgment, merchant aggregation, provenance records, and channel release in a workflow that is more valuable and founder-compatible than a horizontal merchant field store.
evaluation_diagnostics.primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that responsible-person firms have enough costly, recurring dossier work to support attractive pricing and contribution after integration, rule maintenance, support, and qualified review, or that they will embed an external vendor rather than build or bundle the capability.
evaluation_diagnostics.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Major commerce platforms already provide native or bulk GPSR workflows, while general feed and GPSR products support thousands or unlimited products for roughly EUR 59-89 or USD 79.99 per month; this demonstrates commoditization and price pressure around the record-and-transport layer from which the proposed workflow must clearly separate itself.

evaluation_diagnostics.highest_value_structural_change: Make the first commercial unit a fixed-scope, paid reconciliation benchmark inside one authorized client tenant, with a pre-agreed conversion to the partner licence only if explicit thresholds for accuracy, reviewer hours, deployment effort, and avoided rework are met; this converts the most fragile partner-economics and repeatability assumptions into auditable purchase criteria before building a broad platform.
evaluation_diagnostics.main_structural_strength: The wedge sits between confidential client-held contracts and incumbent compliance systems, addressing mandated relational data quality with auditable, human-approved outputs while preserving the customer's system of record.
evaluation_diagnostics.primary_score_limiter: The model depends simultaneously on unproven outsourcer willingness to pay, repeated end-client authorization, and enough cross-tenant connector reuse to avoid services-heavy economics.

evaluation_diagnostics.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid outsourcer-led pilot spanning at least four authorized client tenants, with measured extraction accuracy, human-review time, reusable-integration share, delivery savings, security and support cost, renewal intent, and contractual permission for the proposed deployment and reusable artifacts.
evaluation_diagnostics.highest_value_structural_change: Constrain the initial product to one incumbent GRC or register ecosystem and one complex financial subsegment, with a standardized connector, an outsourcer agreement that embeds end-client authorization in the normal statement of work, and a minimum active-tenant commitment before custom integrations are accepted.
evaluation_diagnostics.main_structural_strength: A mandatory, operational regulatory workflow contains a genuinely relational evidence problem, and a tenant-local complementary layer could exploit an outsourcer's existing portfolio without replacing trusted systems of record.
evaluation_diagnostics.primary_score_limiter: The business depends on one outsourcer repeatedly obtaining client authorization and deploying a sufficiently reusable integration across several tenants; without that repetition, channel leverage, payback, margins, retention, and the founder-wealth path all deteriorate together.

strongest_candidates.title: Client-Tenant DORA Reconciliation Engine for Compliance Outsourcers

unresolved_evidence: A paid implementation commitment from a responsible-person firm in a named category, accompanied by measured before-and-after dossier labor, review accuracy, throughput, incident volume, channel coverage, contribution margin, acquisition cost, renewal intent, and contractually documented evidence-access and reusable-learning rights.

A paid, time-bounded deployment with a responsible-person firm in one named category showing committed dossier volume, baseline and post-deployment review labor, implementation and support cost, accepted-dossier contribution, channel error rates, alert-match precision and recall, partner acquisition effort, and renewal intent at an agreed price.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid pilot and implementation commitment from a responsible-person firm in a named category, with access rights and qualified-review responsibilities contractually defined. Measured dossier throughput, intake time and error reduction, listing-continuity value, incident frequency, and alert-match precision and recall on real partner cases. Observed price, partner acquisition effort, human-review and support cost, gross margin, payback, renewal intent, and concentration economics. Contractual permission and technical proof for reuse of resolved evidence patterns or confirmed identifiers without misrepresenting reviewer approval as legal certification.
records.primary_score_limiter: The selected category's throughput, partner willingness to embed and pay, and contribution economics after qualified review and support are all unproven.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Major marketplaces already provide native GPSR fields and bulk workflows, while public offers price large-catalog feed management from EUR 59 per month and unlimited-product GPSR API tooling at USD 79.99 per month, showing that substantial parts of the proposed value stack are already commoditized.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid design-partner agreement with an independent auditor or specialist consultancy that specifies implementation ownership and recurring review volume. Before-and-after evidence that the workspace materially reduces review labor or improves defect detection and evidence-pack acceptance on authorized operator data. Observed pricing, deployment and support cost, gross margin, acquisition effort, renewal intent, and customer payback across multiple completed cycles. Written legal and security feasibility for the scoped operator-hosted workflow, including data sufficiency and human-control safeguards.
records.primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that an auditor will adopt and pay for the workspace at a frequency and price that produces repeatable contribution economics.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Mature products such as BetBuddy and GameScanner already provide risk classification, explainability, and intervention support, and regulator-published material describes an installed alternative with concrete pricing; a separate assurance workspace must therefore prove incremental value rather than rely on generic compliance demand.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid pilot with a named partner that contractually controls design or specification release, enforces the gate across a recurring case cohort, and records cases per month, supplier completion, labour and cycle-time savings, error or rework reduction, accepted price, onboarding and exception-support cost, contribution margin, renewal intent, and client data-use rights.
records.primary_score_limiter: The buyer, control point, and economic engine are jointly unproven: no identified partner is shown to have both authority to enforce the gate and enough recurring cases to support attractive pricing, margins, renewal, and a founder-scale wealth path.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Low-priced direct competitors already publish compliance tiers containing adjacent declarations, grades, market sheets, and API functions, while official portals handle filing; this evidence narrows monetizable value to demonstrable workflow savings and makes an unsupported software premium or broad feature moat implausible.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid pilot should include written partner and end-client authorization and measure baseline versus post-deployment remediation hours, extraction and reconciliation accuracy, human-review time, assurance and integration cost, and connector reuse; the strongest evidence would be the same partner activating at least four tenants and renewing at the proposed price with positive measured payback.
records.primary_score_limiter: The model's distribution, margins, retention, and defensibility all depend on the same unproven condition: an outsourcer must obtain client authorization and repeat sufficiently standardized integrations across enough tenants to justify the licence and support burden.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Transparent incumbents already offer inexpensive DORA validation and regulator-ready exports, one also overlaps contract-clause analysis, and the dry-run evidence shows many deficient registers failed only a small fraction of checks; this weakens the case for a large, durable, differentiated reconciliation budget.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid design partnership with a confirmed non-exempt OEM; contractual telemetry, processor, and reuse rights; observed request and exception volumes; measured implementation and support hours; and evidence of gross margin, retention intent, and a repeatable partner acquisition route.
records.primary_score_limiter: The necessary telemetry authorization and customer access are controlled by OEM and IoT-platform gatekeepers that can buy an established specialist or bundle the capability themselves, preventing an independent wedge from easily compounding.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Steelbridge already markets almost the same consent, third-party access, API, audit, and white-label layer at public prices near the proposed base fee, while IoT platforms advertise native Data Act functionality.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid agency or responsible-person pilot; complete API-field mapping for the initial channels; measured document-review cost and alert-match precision and recall; proof of reduced listing downtime or incident labor; and cohort evidence for pricing, retention, and agency payback.
records.primary_score_limiter: The proposed premium workflow sits above cheap feed products and native marketplace functionality, yet its differentiating verification and incident work is labor-intensive and has no demonstrated willingness to pay or accuracy advantage.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: eBay, Shopify, and Etsy already support GPSR data workflows, while Channable and a GPSR Shopify app publicly serve large catalogs at prices far below the proposed per-SKU economics.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A contractually authorized PSP or AP-platform design partner; paid pilots with measured exception rates and resolution time; proof of fraud-loss or labor reduction beyond the free result; security and legal feasibility; and validated partner costs, gross margin, retention, and enterprise acquisition payback.
records.primary_score_limiter: Essential data access and customer distribution depend on PSP, bank, or AP-platform partners that already control the workflow and can choose an incumbent, bundle the exception layer, or withhold the interface.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: SurePay already supplies bulk APIs, white-label portals, audit-oriented workflow, broad bank connectivity, and massive verification intelligence, and AIB demonstrates that a bank can distribute that corporate workflow natively.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Two or more paid operator pilots should show lawful access to usable intervention and follow-up data, materially fewer QA defects or manual-review hours, an outcome metric accepted by an independent safer-gambling expert, and willingness to sign an annual contract at the proposed price after security review.
records.primary_score_limiter: The proposed layer has not shown standalone willingness to pay or a hard-to-copy advantage beside mature risk and intervention suites, while acquiring the sensitive data needed to prove value raises procurement and governance friction.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: BetBuddy and Mindway already sell operator-wide detection, explainability, and intervention support, and the regulator does not yet collect interaction quality or impact data, so neither product differentiation nor a separate mandated budget is established.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Three paid pilots in a sharply defined packaging segment should document supplier response and BOM completeness, at least one avoided correction or redesign or a measured 25 to 60 hours saved, renewal intent at the proposed price, and a converter or EPR-adviser channel willing to bring additional accounts.
records.primary_score_limiter: It has not established that brands will pay a durable premium for governed change control above low-cost compliance trackers and free official portals, especially when supplier evidence may remain incomplete.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: PPWR Connect and PackComply already advertise overlapping functions at EUR 29 to EUR 299 per month, while key PPWR grading and fee-modulation methods still depend on future acts, undermining both near-term differentiation and authoritative simulation.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid partner or complex-group pilot should secure approved contract access, demonstrate high field-level accuracy with bounded human-review time, prevent a failed validation or remove 40 to 100 analyst hours, pass the buyer's security review, and convert to recurring use triggered by real contract updates.
records.primary_score_limiter: The differentiation is narrow and unvalidated in a price-anchored category where incumbents already offer validation, exports, audit trails, and some contract analysis, while the proposed product's access to confidential contracts creates additional procurement friction.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Several tools already provide regulator-ready register workflows at transparent low prices, Venvera advertises contract-clause checking, and most dry-run failures involved fewer than five of 116 checks, suggesting many buyers may need only modest episodic remediation.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Two paid OEM pilots should show signed recurring terms, implementation time, measured reduction in duplicate entry and support incidents, production activation across multiple downstream operators, six-month customer payback, and positive contribution margin after partner share, specialist exceptions, and incident support; a corridor-level count of addressable vendors and operators is also needed.
records.primary_score_limiter: There is no demonstrated vendor-channel demand or contribution economics, and the intended channel partners are also well positioned to use cheap incumbents or internalize the connector.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: A no-fee Commission GUI and mature products from Travas, Axians, and ZEDAL already cover the workflow at low prices, while the Commission estimates only EUR 1.4 million in total annual DIWASS administrative savings.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid governed-site pilots need to document current report and dispute costs, dual-party acceptance, authorized data completeness, reviewer hours and liability terms, reduction in revision cycles, one-reporting-cycle payback, annual contribution margin after expert work, and a verified count of active EPC sites controlled by reachable channel partners.
records.primary_score_limiter: The addressable EPC-site base, software budget owner, willingness to pay, and reviewer economics are all unknown, while neutrality requires multi-party adoption that makes distribution and implementation unusually difficult.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: No rule mandates a separate software service; the Polish model assigns reporting to the ESCO, KAPE already bundles settlement control, and low-cost RETScreen plus established EnergyCAP capabilities constrain standalone software value.
